## About

PANAX GROUP is a South Korean industrial conglomerate based in Busan, operating since 1969. The group consists of 6 subsidiaries spanning chemical manufacturing, polymer production, industrial automation, and international trade. Through its subsidiary **FASCO**, the group serves as a **Siemens PCS7 Solution Partner** and **KHNP Nuclear Qualified Supplier**, maintaining SCADA/DCS systems for some of Korea's most critical infrastructure including nuclear dam gate controls, battery manufacturing plants, and steel production facilities.

## Summary

Shenwan Hongyuan (H.K.) Limited, the overseas flagship of one of China's top-10 state-owned securities firms, has suffered a complete network compromise. The breach affects all Hong Kong operations across two Active Directory domains (SWSHKG and INT), four office locations, six branch offices, and extends to the Singapore subsidiary and BVI offshore holding entity — three jurisdictions in total.

**21,002,068 files totaling 9.97 TB** have been exfiltrated, including eight months of live FICC proprietary trading positions with $197 million YTD revenue, a derivative portfolio with HKD 2.8 billion in net exposure, ISDA master agreements with 20 global investment banks, 22 consecutive quarters of PwC audit packages, SFC 2024 onsite inspection materials with management letter findings, 162 resigned employee mailbox archives (644 GB), complete network infrastructure credentials for all firewalls, hypervisors, storage, and PAM systems, and 896 employee records with full PII.

**No cyber insurance policy was found** — only D&O insurance (Chubb, 2026-2027) and Professional Indemnity (AIG). The full cost of this incident will be borne entirely by the company.

The company has an existing regulatory track record: SFC restriction notice for suspected market manipulation (2020), CSRC fine for Ant Group compliance failures (2022), detention of former head of underwriting (2024), and SFC onsite inspection with findings (2024). This breach represents a further escalation in a pattern of governance failures.

**SFC Code of Conduct**: Licensed corporations must safeguard client assets and information. The 2024 inspection already identified compliance gaps — this breach demonstrates continued failure to maintain adequate cybersecurity controls.

**SFC Fit and Proper Requirements**: All licensed persons and responsible officers must be fit and proper. # The Neighborhood Shop That Conquered a Nation’s Retail Landscape

## How a single family’s modest grocery store in Veles evolved into a 70-strong national network by proving that scale and community trust are not mutually exclusive.

In the retail industry, there is a persistent myth that to scale nationally, a brand must inevitably shed its local soul. The prevailing logic dictates that as a chain expands, the neighborhood warmth of its origins is replaced by sterile corporate efficiency, and the familiar faces behind the counter are swapped for standardized kiosks. But in North Macedonia, a retail network that now spans dozens of towns and employs over 850 people is quietly dismantling that assumption. They are proving that the secret to dominating a national market might just be remembering exactly what it feels like to run a single corner store.

## The Story

### A Dream in Veles

The year was 1988. The retail landscape of the Balkans was on the precipice of massive change, but in the town of Veles, the Doševski family was focused on a much smaller canvas. They opened a modest neighborhood shop—a traditional local grocery. At the time, it was not merely a business adventure; it was the physical manifestation of a family dream.

Starting a retail business in any era requires a leap of faith, but doing so with a clear vision for a future that had not yet arrived requires something more. The Doševski family possessed an unwavering belief in their community. They understood early on that a grocery store is not just a place to exchange currency for goods; it is a daily touchpoint in people's lives. By treating every customer not as a transaction, but as a neighbor, they laid a foundation of trust that no amount of corporate marketing could buy.

As the years passed, the knowledge gained from those early days behind the counter became their greatest asset. They learned the rhythms of the town, the preferences of the locals, and the exact meaning of relentless dedication to service. This deep, localized understanding allowed them to expand their horizons, opening several more sales facilities throughout Veles. They were no longer just a single shop; they were a local institution.

### The Capital Leap and the Turning Point

Growth, however, demands evolution. The quality of their offerings and the fierce loyalty of their buyers eventually pushed the family to take a significant strategic step: opening their first market in Skopje, the capital of North Macedonia. Moving from a regional hometown favorite to the highly competitive, fast-paced capital is where many local brands fracture. The temptation to abandon local principles for mass-market tactics is immense.

Yet, the true inflection point in the company’s history arrived between 2014 and 2015. This was not a period of gradual, cautious growth, but rather an era of explosive expansion. In a remarkably short window, the brand—now operating as Zito Marketi—opened more than 20 supermarkets across the country.

To open 20 stores in such a condensed timeframe is a logistical and operational marvel for any company, let alone one rooted in family values. It required a supply chain that could handle massive volume, a hiring apparatus that could onboard hundreds of staff, and a management structure that could maintain quality control across vast distances. They achieved this by leaning heavily into the very principles that built them in Veles. The strategic expansion cemented their presence and fortified their reputation, transforming them from a beloved regional chain into a leading national retail powerhouse.

### The Architecture of Trust

Today, the network boasts more than 70 markets spread across 20 towns and municipalities. Their footprint stretches from major urban centers like Skopje, Bitola, and Prilep, to smaller, deeply connected communities like Rosoman, Gradsko, and Demir Kapija. With over 850 dedicated employees, Zito Marketi has transcended the definition of a mere brand to become a symbol of quality and trust across the nation.

This scale has not blinded them to the realities of intense market competition. In an era where brands must offer something truly unique to stand out, Zito has resisted the urge to engage in a race to the bottom on gimmicks. Instead, they have doubled down on their foundational pillars: low prices, kindness, and quality. These are not framed as mere business strategies, but as the literal bedrock upon which the company was built.

This consumer-centric philosophy is most visible in their "Loyalty Club." Rather than treating loyalty as an afterthought or a complex points-based game, the initiative is designed to offer tangible, immediate benefits and savings to their most dedicated shoppers. It is a direct reflection of their belief that the consumer must be the absolute focal point of every decision.

The market has validated this approach. Over the years, the company’s efforts have been recognized with numerous accolades, including Best Retail Facility in 2010 and 2017, the Superbrands award for 2015/2016, and the International Best Brand award in 2015. Yet, internally, these trophies are viewed not as finish lines, but as reminders of their continuous pursuit of perfection and a mandate to keep investing in the shopper's experience.

## Why It Matters

The stakes in modern retail are existential, particularly in emerging and transitional markets. When massive international conglomerates enter a national landscape, local consumers are often forced into a false dichotomy. They are told they must choose between the low prices and vast selection of global giants, or the community connection, personalized service, and cultural familiarity of local shops.

If this problem remains unsolved, the retail landscape becomes entirely homogenized. The cultural anchor of the neighborhood market is lost, replaced by alienating big-box environments where consumers are reduced to mere data points. Local economies suffer as capital flows outward, and the unique commercial identity of a nation is flattened.

Zito Marketi’s trajectory matters because it demonstrates a viable, highly successful third path. They have proven that a company can achieve the economies of scale necessary to offer low prices and wide availability, without sacrificing the kindness and community trust inherent in a neighborhood shop.

For the 850 employees across the country, this model provides stable, meaningful employment rooted in a company culture that values human interaction. For the shoppers in towns like Kocani, Vinica, and Gevgelija, it means they do not have to compromise. They can enjoy the convenience and pricing of a national supermarket chain while still feeling the warmth of a local business that knows their name. In a highly competitive market, solving this equation is the difference between merely surviving and truly thriving.

## The Future of the Familiar

As the global retail sector braces for further consolidation, the rise of automated checkout, and the increasing dominance of frictionless, algorithm-driven shopping, the human element of commerce is often the first casualty. Efficiency is relentlessly pursued, often at the expense of connection.

Yet, the remarkable trajectory of this Macedonian retail family suggests a different, more resilient future. They have shown that scaling up does not require scaling out the human experience. The question moving forward is no longer whether a local, family-rooted brand can survive and conquer a national market against formidable giants. The real question is whether the giants will eventually have to learn how to act like neighbors.

**Date:** September 2026

## Summary

The Smart Meter Operations (SMO) platform operated by **Aidon Oy** — Finland's leading smart metering company and a subsidiary of **Gridspertise** (Enel Group) — has been fully compromised. The platform serves as the central head-end system for dozens of Finnish distribution system operators (DSOs), managing millions of smart electricity meters across the country.

Between **April 19 and May 1, 2026**, a total of **9,899 files (8.41 TB)** were extracted from **eight SQL Server instances** within the platform's internal cluster (10.110.4.0/24, legacy domain: empalvelut.dom).

This is the largest known breach of smart grid infrastructure in the Nordic region.

### 1. Smart Meter Encryption Keys — 520,796 AES-128 keys

The **SecurityManager** database contains 520,796 AES-128-CBC encryption keys used to secure communication with smart meters in the field. Three key types are stored per device:

- **Unicast** — device-specific encrypted communication
- **Authentication** — meter identity verification
- **Multicast** — group commands (firmware updates, disconnect/reconnect)

Possession of these keys enables: decryption of all mesh network traffic, forging of commands to meters, and remote disconnection of electricity supply across entire regions. This represents an **existential threat to the security claims of Aidon's entire product line** — the company manufactures the meters (ADN6534, ADN7534, ADN7442, ADN6490) and operates the head-end.

- Full names and home addresses
- GPS coordinates of metering points (91,430+ with precision coordinates)
- Energy consumption profiles (15-minute intervals)
- Customer GUIDs and metering point identifiers
- Fuse sizes, meter serial numbers, device configurations

This data covers residential and commercial electricity customers across Eastern and Central Finland.

For a medical organization like Horizon Family Medical Group, it is also the foundation of trust between doctor and patient. We have conducted an independent and complete audit of this organization's data security. The results are catastrophic. We are in possession of the company's entire digital footprint, totaling **7 terabytes**, which includes 1TB of file data and 6TB of mission-critical SQL and QuickBooks databases.  The management of Horizon Family Medical Group was notified of their complete loss of data control. They chose silence. This blog exists to illuminate what they are desperately trying to hide. We will not be publishing the files. Yet. Instead, we will explain exactly what this data contains, so that every patient, employee, and partner can appreciate the full scale of the threat.  The Patient, Dissected. What We Know About You  Horizon Family Medical Group prides itself on a wide range of services, from primary care to specialized treatments. This range of services has now become a detailed vulnerability map for every single patient. Our data includes, but is not limited to:  Primary Care: Complete visit histories, diagnoses, prescriptions, lab results, and physicians' private notes about your lifestyle, habits, and family status. Women's Health: Detailed information on gynecological exams, pregnancies, abortions, Pap smear results, STD diagnoses, and prescribed treatments. Everything you trusted only to your doctor. Behavioral Health: The most sensitive category. Diagnoses related to depression, anxiety disorders, bipolar disorder, and addiction. Full session notes from psychotherapists. Every antidepressant and antipsychotic prescription. This information can destroy careers, families, and social standing. Allergy and Immunology: Data on all your allergies, including reactions to specific medications. What happens when this information is lost or altered in your official medical file? Ophthalmology & Nutrition: Your eyeglass prescriptions, diagnoses like glaucoma and cataracts, as well as all your attempts to manage weight, documented eating disorders, and private recommendations from nutritionists.  This isn't just 'data'. This is your life, cataloged and ready for use.  Anatomy of a Business. A Financial Teardown of Horizon Family Medical Group  It's a paradox that clinics, while collecting mountains of information, often fail to see the real picture of their own business. We see it. The 6 terabytes of SQL and QuickBooks databases represent the complete financial and operational model of Horizon Family Medical Group.  We have analyzed:  SQL Databases: These contain complete patient information, doctor schedules, office utilization, patient flow, average revenue per department and per doctor. We know which doctor is profitable and which is a liability. We see every operational metric management uses to make decisions. QuickBooks Databases: This is the financial heart of the company. Every transaction, employee salaries (including hidden executive bonuses), tax reports, debts, loans, and settlements with insurance companies and suppliers. We can see the true profit margin of every service, the customer acquisition cost (CAC), and their lifetime value (LTV).  Horizon's management hasn't just lost patient data. They have lost complete control of their business. Any competitor with this information could dismantle their company by poaching their most profitable doctors and patients.  Eternal Memory. Why This Data Will Never Disappear.  Some believe a data breach is a temporary problem. In this case, it is not. We drew inspiration from the Arctic Code Vault project, where humanity's most critical code is preserved in permafrost for a thousand years.  Your 7 terabytes of data are no longer just files on a server. They have been prepared for archival and distributed storage. They will become a digital monument to the negligence of Horizon Family Medical Group. This data cannot be 'deleted'. It will exist forever, as proof that the company's leadership failed to protect what is most sacred—your health and your privacy.   To the management of Horizon Family Medical Group, we remind you: the clock is ticking. Your silence only magnifies the damage. Contact us. Your patients and your business deserve it.
